title: Why Doubling Credit Card Debt Quadruples the Interest

beats.say: Same $300 a month at 24%: $3,000 costs $381 in interest. $6,000 costs $1,739.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a sleek black card sitting on rain-slicked dark asphalt under red sodium streetlights.

beats.say: Double the balance doesn't mean double the interest cost. It quadruples it completely.
beats.visual: Low angle of massive concrete urban towers rising into heavy night fog.

beats.say: Most people assume paying off a $6,000 balance takes twice as long as paying $3,000.
beats.visual: High angle silhouette of a lone person walking along a rusted metal industrial bridge.

beats.say: That's wrong. You're actually trapped paying for 26 full months instead of just 12.
beats.visual: Wide shot of an empty subway platform under pale flickering fluorescent light.

beats.say: Here's why fixed payments turn vicious the moment your card balance doubles.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of heavy iron gears inside an ancient clock tower in shadow.

beats.say: With a $3,000 balance at 24%, your $300 payment cuts heavy principal from month one.
beats.visual: Silhouette of hands opening a heavy steel vault door under low amber light.

beats.say: You wipe out the debt in 12 months and keep total interest at just $381.
beats.visual: Wide shot of a solitary streetlight gleaming on wet pavement during blue hour.

beats.say: So why does that exact same $300 monthly payment stall when debt hits $6,000?
beats.visual: Extreme wide angle of a dark abandoned warehouse floor lit by a single overhead lamp.

beats.say: Because at $6,000, interest steals nearly half of your payment in the early months.
beats.visual: Low angle looking up a spiraling dark concrete stairwell in dim sodium glow.

beats.say: Your principal balance barely drops, locking you into the debt for 14 additional months.
beats.visual: High angle silhouette of a figure standing on a towering skyscraper ridge in heavy mist.

beats.say: That slow decay forces you to keep bleeding interest every single month you wait.
beats.visual: Close-up of water dripping off a rusted steel cable in dark blue night light.

beats.say: That's how doubling your debt skyrockets your interest cost from $381 all the way to $1,739.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a glowing red neon light reflecting off wet asphalt.

beats.say: Fixed payments hide the real math. Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Wide shot of a dark empty highway extending into dense morning fog at dawn.

caption:
Why $6,000 of card debt costs over 4x more interest than $3,000 at the same monthly payment. The math of card payoffs.

#money #personalfinance #creditcard #debttips #mathofmoney
description: When you double your credit card debt, keeping the same fixed monthly payment doesn't just double your payoff time—it quadruples your total interest expense. Learn how fixed payments create a slow-decay trap on larger balances.
first_comment: Did you realize fixed card payments cost this much extra interest on higher balances?

facts.claim: A $3,000 card balance at 24% APR paid at $300/month takes 12 months and costs $381 in total interest.
facts.basis: Money Fact Sheet: $3,000 credit card at 24% APR paying $300/month: 12 months, $381 interest.

facts.claim: A $6,000 card balance at 24% APR paid at $300/month takes 26 months and costs $1,739 in total interest.
facts.basis: Money Fact Sheet: $6,000 credit card at 24% APR paying $300/month: 26 months, $1,739 interest.

loop_map.stakes: Doubling a credit card balance on a fixed monthly payment quadruples your interest expense.
loop_map.big_question: Why does doubling a card balance from $3,000 to $6,000 multiply your interest cost by over four times?
loop_map.assume: Paying off $6,000 at $300/month will take twice as long and cost double the interest of paying off $3,000.
loop_map.reveal: Higher starting interest consumes half the payment early on, dragging out the timeline by 14 extra months and exploding total interest to $1,739.
